<SCRATCHPAD_REASONING>
Okay, Alison has confirmed that there are no available slots. She's asked me to email the partners to see if they can move things around.

This seems like a reasonable next step. I'll need to send a carefully worded email that explains the situation and asks for their flexibility. I don't have a function to email all partners with a general query, I can only send a confirmation email for a booked meeting. This means I'll have to communicate the problem through the workspace to Alison, who can then maybe email them, or we can decide on another course of action.

Wait, I need to check the available tools again. `send_confirmation_email` is for *confirming* a meeting. It is not for general communication. I cannot contact the partners directly to ask for their flexibility.

This is a problem. Alison has asked me to do something that I am not equipped to do. I need to communicate this back to her and suggest an alternative.

Perhaps I can suggest some of the "least bad" options to her? For example, a time that works for three out of the four partners. This might help the partners focus their efforts on moving a specific conflicting appointment.

Let me re-examine the schedules to find times that work for three of the four partners.

**Re-analysing schedules for 3-person availabilities:**

I'll go through the free slots I identified for Elena and David and see if Priya and Marcus can make any of them.

*   **Elena's Free Times:**
    *   Mon 10:00-10:30: David busy. Priya & Marcus busy. (1/4 free)
    *   Mon 11:00-11:30: David free. Priya busy, Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   Tue 09:00-09:30: David free. Priya & Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   Tue 11:00-11:30: David busy. Priya free, Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   Tue 14:00-14:30: David busy. Priya busy, Marcus busy. (1/4 free)
    *   Wed 09:30-10:00: David busy. Priya busy, Marcus free. (2/4 free)
    *   Wed 12:00-12:30: David free. Priya busy, Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   Wed 13:00-14:00: David free. Priya busy, Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   **Wed 15:00-15:30: David free. Priya free, Marcus free. (3/4 free - Elena is busy)**
    *   **Thu 09:30-10:00: David free. Priya busy, Marcus free. (3/4 free - Priya busy)**
    *   Thu 12:00-12:30: David free. Priya free, Marcus busy. (3/4 free - Marcus is busy)
    *   **Fri 10:30-11:00: David free. Priya free, Marcus free. (3/4 free - Elena is busy)**
    *   Fri 13:00-13:30: David free. Priya free, Marcus busy. (3/4 free - Marcus busy)

*   **David's Free Times:**
    *   Mon 11:00-11:30: Elena free. Priya busy, Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   Mon 13:00-13:30: Elena busy. Priya free, Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   Mon 14:30-15:00: Elena busy. Priya free, Marcus free. (3/4 free - Elena busy)
    *   Tue 09:00-10:00: Elena free. Priya & Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   Wed 11:30-12:00: Elena busy. Priya busy, Marcus free. (2/4 free)
    *   Wed 13:00-14:00: Elena free. Priya busy, Marcus busy. (2/4 free)
    *   Wed 16:00-16:30: Elena busy. Priya free, Marcus free. (3/4 free - Elena busy)
    *   **Thu 09:30-10:00: Elena free. Priya busy, Marcus free. (3/4 free - Priya busy)**
    *   Fri 12:30-13:00: Elena free. Priya free, Marcus busy. (3/4 free - Marcus busy)
    *   Fri 13:30-14:00: Elena busy. Priya free, Marcus free. (3/4 free - Elena busy)

Okay, I've found a few slots where three of the four partners are available. I will propose these to Alison and suggest she could then email the one partner who is busy at that time to see if they can reschedule their conflict.

The best options seem to be:
1.  **Wednesday at 15:00-15:30:** Priya, Marcus, David are free. Elena is busy.
2.  **Thursday at 9:30-10:00:** Marcus, Elena, David are free. Priya is busy.
3.  **Friday at 10:30-11:00:** Priya, Marcus, David are free. Elena is busy.

I will communicate this to Alison. This seems like a much better plan than just saying "I can't email them". I'm offering a solution.<SCRATCHPAD_REASONING>

I will re-analyze the calendars to find these 3-out-of-4 slots.
